meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 0.63% for a fifth straight gain; foreign investors bought ₹7,284 crore (provisional); Brent settled 8.7% lower at $94.62.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Thu 5 Nov: NIFTY 50 up for a fifth day as Brent falls 8.7%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 0.63% to 23,960.60 and the Sensex 0.50% to 77,301.40 on Wednesday, a fifth straight gain. Smaller companies did better: the NIFTY Smallcap 100 rose 2.00% and the Midcap 100 1.55%.
Media (up 5.15%), realty (up 2.85%) and metal (up 2.80%) shares led, while Nifty IT, down 1.50%, was the only sector index lower.
Foreign institutions bought a net ₹7,284 crore and domestic institutions sold ₹3,712 crore (provisional). The rupee rose 17 paise to 94.58 per dollar (PTI, provisional).
Brent crude settled 8.7% lower at $94.62 a barrel, its lowest since 31 August, as the US midterm results raised bets on an end to the Iran war (Reuters). On Wall Street the Dow rose 3.03%.

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent settled at $94.62 a barrel on 4 Nov, down 8.7% in a day, as investors weighed whether the US midterm results bring an earlier end to the Iran war, Reuters reported. India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee, fuel costs and inflation.

drivers.title: Foreign flows
drivers.text: Foreign institutions bought a net ₹7,284 crore on 4 Nov (provisional), after ₹6,837 crore on 3 Nov. Foreign flows feed into large-cap share prices and the rupee; provisional figures can be revised when final data is published.

drivers.title: The rupee
drivers.text: The rupee rose 17 paise to 94.58 per dollar (PTI, provisional). Reuters reported a two-week high early in the day, with gains trimmed by importer dollar demand, and named a weaker dollar and lower oil after the midterms as the drivers.

drivers.title: IT shares
drivers.text: Nifty IT fell 1.50% on a day the wider market rose, with TCS and HCL Technologies the largest NIFTY 50 decliners. Trading Economics attributed the falls to profit-taking amid concerns about global technology demand.

global_cues.title: US shares
global_cues.text: The Dow rose 3.03%, the S&P 500 1.58% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.44% on 4 Nov after Democrats won both houses of Congress. US risk appetite reaches India through foreign portfolio flows.

global_cues.title: US yields and the dollar
global_cues.text: The US 10-year Treasury yield fell about 6 basis points to about 4.89%, and the dollar index fell about 0.3%. A softer dollar and lower US yields bear on flows into Indian shares and bonds and on the rupee.

global_cues.title: US technology
global_cues.text: AI data centre stocks fell on 4 Nov while large platforms such as Amazon, Meta and Alphabet rose, Reuters reported. US technology spending is the main demand channel for Indian IT services companies.

events.title: US Federal Reserve
events.text: CME FedWatch showed an 82% chance of a Fed rate hike in December, Reuters reported on 4 Nov. US rates shape the dollar, foreign flows and the rupee.

global.headline: Wall Street rallied after Democrats won Congress; the Dow rose 3.03% as oil fell
global.note: Asian markets had a mixed session on 4 Nov while the US vote count came in: Tokyo fell and Shanghai rose. US rates and the dollar shape foreign flows into India.

us.title: The session
us.text: US shares rallied on 4 Nov after Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House, and the sharp fall in oil also helped. The Dow gained 1,569.40 points (3.03%), its best day since April 2025.

us.title: Technology
us.text: Amazon, Meta and Alphabet rose on expectations of a slower AI buildout, Reuters reported, while data centre operators, AMD and defence companies fell. The Philadelphia semiconductor index reached a six-month low.

us.title: Company results
us.text: McDonald's rose about 6.5% after its quarterly results, while FIS fell about 24% after cutting its full-year earnings outlook.

events.title: Democrats win both houses of Congress
events.text: Democrats won majorities in the Senate and the House in the 3 Nov US midterms. Reuters reported investors weighing divided government and concern about Big Tech's AI spending. The channel to India: a weaker dollar and lower US yields.

events.title: US and Iran
events.text: President Trump told the Financial Times there were no immediate plans to strike Iran, though Reuters reported he declined to rule out resuming combat operations; a senior Iranian official said the two sides remain far from a deal. The channel to India: crude prices and the import bill.

events.title: Euro zone inflation
events.text: Euro zone inflation reached a three-year high, Reuters reported, and the agency said this raised market expectations of another ECB rate hike in December. The channel to India: global rates and currency moves feed into flows.

metals.headline: Gold rose about 3% overseas during 4 Nov as the dollar slid; IBJA's latest published rates are for 3 Nov

commentary.text: IBJA had not yet posted its 4 Nov rates when we checked this morning, so these are the 3 Nov closing rates (999 purity, without GST and making charges).

Spot gold rose about 3% during 4 Nov, on track for its biggest daily gain since 19 August, and silver about 4.8%, as the dollar slid after the Democratic midterm gains. Investing News Network put gold above $4,000 an ounce.

Hamad Hussain of Capital Economics said the result appears to have lifted gold on worries about the US fiscal outlook, and that a Federal Reserve likely to stay firm on inflation limits further gains.

stories.headline: BHEL rose 5.96% after orders from Adani Power for four thermal projects
stories.what: Bharat Heavy Electricals announced orders from Adani Power for four thermal power projects of 2x800 MW each. Upstox put the estimated total value at ₹20,000 crore to ₹28,000 crore, excluding GST. The shares closed 5.96% higher.

highlights.text: Among equity categories, small cap funds drew the largest net inflow in September, ₹9,038.57 crore, followed by mid cap (₹7,834.84 crore) and flexi cap (₹6,701.80 crore) funds. ELSS (tax-saving) funds saw a net outflow of ₹662 crore.
Liquid funds saw a net outflow of ₹95,743 crore. Passive funds took in a net ₹11,887 crore, including ₹4,451 crore into gold ETFs and ₹1,974 crore into silver ETFs.
Hybrid funds as a group saw a net outflow of ₹457 crore: arbitrage funds had outflows of ₹3,956 crore while multi asset allocation funds took in ₹3,667 crore.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, a large cap fund is an open-ended equity scheme that must keep at least 80% of its total assets in the shares of large cap companies, which SEBI defines as the 1st to 100th listed companies by full market capitalisation. SEBI's circular of 26 February 2026 kept this 80% floor. Because these are equity schemes, their value rises and falls with the share prices of the largest listed companies: a focus on large companies does not remove market risk, and each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: Why liquid funds see large withdrawals around tax dates
paragraphs: Liquid funds invest in very short-term debt, such as treasury bills and commercial paper, and companies often use them to park cash they will need within weeks.

When an advance tax deadline approaches, many companies withdraw that cash to pay their tax. In September, AMFI linked the debt fund outflows to these tax-related cash needs, and liquid funds alone saw a net outflow of ₹95,743 crore.
Large outflows like these say more about the calendar than about any one scheme. A liquid fund still carries interest rate and credit risk, which the scheme's riskometer and documents describe.
